title: Robins-Wang Variance Estimation for Multiply Imputed Data
text: first step impute data using mice. parametric imputation, package supports method = "norm" method = "logreg". calling mice, set tasks = "train" save fitted imputation models needed with_rw() pool_rw(). example uses nhanes data mice package. standardizing variables, creates five imputed datasets using norm method. Use with_rw() fit linear regression bmi age hyp completed dataset. Use pool_rw() combine coefficient estimates compute Robins-Wang standard errors confidence intervals. comparison, Rubin’s rules can applied imputations.
code: library(rw) library(mice)  nhanes_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(nhanes))  set.seed(1) imp_norm <- mice(nhanes_scaled, method = "norm", m = 5,                  tasks = "train", print = FALSE) fit_norm <- with_rw(imp_norm, lm(bmi ~ age + hyp)) pool_rw(fit_norm) #>  #> Robins-Wang pooled results #> ------------------------- #> Number of imputations: 5 #> Sample size: 25 #>  #>         term estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high #>  (Intercept) -0.04751    0.3343   -0.1421  0.8883  -0.7407    0.6457 #>          age -0.45865    0.5336   -0.8596  0.3993  -1.5652    0.6479 #>          hyp  0.17550    1.3955    0.1258  0.9011  -2.7187    3.0697 pool(with(imp_norm, lm(bmi ~ age + hyp))) |>   summary() #>          term    estimate std.error  statistic        df   p.value #> 1 (Intercept) -0.04751093 0.2077719 -0.2286686 15.029658 0.8222087 #> 2         age -0.45864607 0.3618038 -1.2676651  4.179919 0.2709358 #> 3         hyp  0.17549617 0.3683495  0.4764393  3.619564 0.6610792

title: Robins-Wang Variance Estimation for Multiply Imputed Data
text: predictive mean matching, set imputation method "pmmrw" incomplete variable use tasks = "train" mice. method uses PMM donor draw implemented mice saves donor IDs fitted matching models needed variance estimation. correction accounts repeated use donor; change imputed values. example imputes bmi using age predictor, default pool five donors. Next, use with_rw() regress bmi age completed dataset. PMM variable response linear model, pool_rw() computes PMM cross term applies donor-source correction automatically. Using seed method = "pmm" gives completed values. donor IDs used imputation available needed.
code: nhanes_pmm <- nhanes_scaled[c("age", "bmi")]  set.seed(2) imp_pmm <- mice(nhanes_pmm, method = c(age = "", bmi = "pmmrw"),                 m = 5, tasks = "train", print = FALSE) fit_pmm <- with_rw(imp_pmm, lm(bmi ~ age)) pool_rw(fit_pmm) #>  #> Robins-Wang pooled results #> ------------------------- #> Number of imputations: 5 #> Sample size: 25 #>  #>         term estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high #>  (Intercept)   0.1042    0.2422    0.4301  0.6711  -0.3969   0.60524 #>          age  -0.3036    0.1944   -1.5618  0.1320  -0.7057   0.09851 set.seed(2) imp_standard <- mice(nhanes_pmm, method = c(age = "", bmi = "pmm"),                      m = 5, print = FALSE) identical(imp_pmm$imp$bmi, imp_standard$imp$bmi) #> [1] TRUE head(extract_donor_id(imp_pmm, "bmi")) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] #> [1,]    8    8    8   19    9 #> [2,]   NA   NA   NA   NA   NA #> [3,]    7   15    8   22   25 #> [4,]   17    2   22   25    8 #> [5,]   NA   NA   NA   NA   NA #> [6,]   24   20    8   24    5

title: Robins-Wang Variance Estimation for Multiply Imputed Data
text: package includes giganti_data, simulated dataset based Giganti Shepherd (2020). variables D observed validation subsample 1,000 individuals. analysis model logistic regression D , inclusion restricted > 2. parametric imputation, uses normal model D uses logistic regression. predictive mean matching, pmm_kappa_binomial() computes PMM cross term binomial analysis final variance assembled.
code: data("giganti_data", package = "rw") gs <- giganti_data predictors <- c("X1", "X2", "A.star", "D.star")  pred <- make.predictorMatrix(gs) pred[,] <- 0L pred["A", predictors] <- 1L pred["D", c(predictors, "A")] <- 1L method <- make.method(gs) method[] <- "" method[c("A", "D")] <- c("norm", "logreg")  set.seed(41) imp_gs_norm <- mice(gs, m = 2, method = method, predictorMatrix = pred,                     tasks = "train", print = FALSE) fit_gs_norm <- with_rw(   imp_gs_norm,   glm(D ~ A, subset = A > 2, family = binomial()) ) pool_rw(fit_gs_norm) #>  #> Robins-Wang pooled results #> ------------------------- #> Number of imputations: 2 #> Sample size: 4000 #>  #>         term estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low conf.high #>  (Intercept)  -2.9450   0.25162   -11.704 1.211e-31  -3.4382   -2.4519 #>            A   0.6941   0.08243     8.421 3.728e-17   0.5326    0.8557 method[c("A", "D")] <- c("pmmrw", "logreg")  set.seed(42) imp_gs_pmm <- mice(gs, m = 2, method = method, predictorMatrix = pred,                    tasks = "train", print = FALSE) fit_gs_pmm <- with_rw(   imp_gs_pmm,   glm(D ~ A, subset = A > 2, family = binomial()) ) kappa <- pmm_kappa_binomial(fit_gs_pmm, "A", threshold = 2) pool_rw(fit_gs_pmm, pmm_kappa = kappa) #>  #> Robins-Wang pooled results #> ------------------------- #> Number of imputations: 2 #> Sample size: 4000 #>  #>         term estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low conf.high #>  (Intercept)  -3.3101    0.3081   -10.742 6.449e-27  -3.9141   -2.7062 #>            A   0.8014    0.1001     8.008 1.166e-15   0.6053    0.9975

title: Robins-Wang Variance Estimation for Multiply Imputed Data
text: Parametric imputation supports norm logreg lm() binomial glm() analyses. PMM supports one numeric imputed variable fully observed matching predictors. Use pool_rw() untransformed PMM response lm(), pmm_kappa_binomial() binomial setting shown . PMM analyses require expected-score function passed pmm_kappa(). See ?pool_rw ?pmm_kappa supported model structures, ?mice.impute.pmmrw PMM options.

Return one matrix per analysis coefficient, coefficient order. Rows observed donors columns missing recipients, original data order. entry expected score donor-recipient pair, accounting analysis subset downstream imputation. cross term averages scores times probability derivatives imputations divides full sample size. selection probabilities differentiated, expected scores.

title: PMM cross terms — pmm
text: pmm_kappa_binomial() supports unweighted glm(D ~ , family = binomial()) default logit link, optionally using > threshold. uses pmmrw D uses logreg. logistic imputation model must include untransformed additive predictor; predictors must fully observed. score uses observed responses available recorded logistic model otherwise. Quadrature integrates fitted normal donor distribution; change donor pool imputed values.

title: Fit and pool an RW analysis — rw
text: with_rw() retains completed values variable types. Rows excluded analysis subset receive zero analysis scores. Parametric cross terms calculated stored analysis imputation scores. PMM pooling supports one numeric PMM variable fully observed matching-model predictors accounts repeated donor use. Automatic PMM pooling requires untransformed PMM variable lm() response. Analysis predictors subset must depend fully observed variables. analyses need matrix pmm_kappa pmm_kappa_binomial. summary() reports standard errors, tests 95% confidence intervals. uses first fitted model's residual degrees freedom lm() normal distribution binomial glm().
